# Path to Five Nines
- - Invest in reliability
- - Empower teams to own quality
- - Build a culture of operational excellence
-
- (circulated to 200 engineers. a quarter later, nothing has changed)
+ ## Diagnosis
+ We miss reliability targets because **no team can see its own reliability until
+ an incident review.** There are no SLOs, so "reliable enough" is decided after
+ the fact by whoever is in the room. Three consequences we can trace:
+ - 4 of the last 6 incidents were caused by a dependency the owning team did not
+   know it had. Nothing maps service → dependency → blast radius.
+ - Reliability work competes with features on vibes, so it loses every planning
+   cycle. It has no unit of measure to compete with.
+ - On-call rotations are per-team and unstaffed below 5 engineers; 4 teams are
+   below that, which means 1-deep rotations and no time to fix causes.
+
+ This is about the system, not the teams. Every one of those teams is making a
+ locally rational choice given what they can see.
+
+ ## Guiding policy
+ **Every tier-1 service gets an SLO and an error budget before it gets new
+ features. Budget spent = reliability work takes priority, automatically.**
+ We are buying one thing: a decision rule that doesn't need a meeting.
+
+ ## Coherent actions (Monday-legible)
+ 1. Platform ships SLO tooling + dependency mapping. Q1. Not a team's job.
+ 2. The 12 tier-1 services define SLOs with the platform team, 2 hours each. Q1.
+ 3. Rotations below 5 engineers merge into 3 shared rotations. Q2. This is the
+    unpopular one and it is not optional.
+ 4. Planning template gains one required line: budget consumed last quarter.
+
+ ## What we are NOT doing
+ Not chasing five nines. Two tier-1 services need 99.9%; the rest are 99.5% and
+ saying so out loud frees real capacity. The old title was the first mistake.

caption.en: "Path to Five Nines" and its three bullets, rewritten as a diagnosis someone could act on Monday.
caption.es: "Camino a los cinco nueves" y sus tres viñetas, reescritas como un diagnóstico que alguien pueda accionar el lunes.

note.en: Three goals, zero diagnosis. Nobody can disagree with them, which is why nothing happened.
note.es: Tres metas, cero diagnóstico. Nadie puede discrepar, y por eso no pasó nada.

note.en: The diagnosis names a mechanism. That's what makes actions derivable instead of arbitrary.
note.es: El diagnóstico nombra un mecanismo. Eso hace que las acciones se deriven en vez de ser arbitrarias.

note.en: The diagnosis is the political part. Write it honestly about the system, or it reads as blame.
note.es: El diagnóstico es la parte política. Escríbelo honestamente sobre el sistema, o se lee como culpa.

note.en: A strategy with no unpopular action isn't allocating anything scarce.
note.es: Una estrategia sin una acción impopular no está asignando nada escaso.

note.en: "Five nines" was an aspiration nobody costed. Naming the real targets is what returns capacity.
note.es: "Cinco nueves" era una aspiración sin costear. Nombrar los objetivos reales es lo que devuelve capacidad.

# 15 minutes, VP of Engineering staff meeting — payments monolith

## Way 1: the update (what most people bring)
- 0-6 min   How the monolith is structured, with a diagram
- 6-11 min  Everything that's hard about it: deploy coupling, test time, on-call
- 11-14 min "So there are a few options: extract payments, strangler pattern,
            or invest in test speed. What do you think?"
- 14-15 min VP: "Come back with a recommendation." Nothing decided.

Two failures. It builds up to the point instead of leading with it, and it hands
a question upward without a pick.

## Way 2: the ask (what I brought)
- 0-1 min   **"I'm asking you to approve 3 engineers for 2 quarters to extract
            payments from the monolith. Here's why, and here's what it costs."**
- 1-4 min   Why now: payment deploys are blocked behind the monolith's 90-minute
            test suite, so we ship payment fixes twice a week instead of daily.
            The two incidents in Q2 both had fixes ready inside 20 minutes.
- 4-8 min   What I considered and rejected: test-suite investment gets us to ~40
            minutes, which doesn't change the shipping cadence; full
            decomposition is 6+ quarters and we don't need it.
- 8-12 min  Cost, risk, and what I'd stop doing to fund it.
- 12-15 min Questions.

## Adapting to the room
Same content, different delivery per leader — this is preparation, not politics:
- **Pre-reader:** doc 24h ahead; the meeting is objections only. Walking the slides
  at someone who has read them is an insult dressed as thoroughness.
- **Think-out-loud:** bring the recommendation and the two rejected options, and
  expect to re-derive it together. Don't defend; think with them.
- **Number-first:** cost, headcount and expected effect in the first sentence.

## The one rule for pushback
Capture it and follow up with data. Do not fight it in the room — you will spend
your credibility defending an estimate instead of getting a decision. "Let me get
you the deploy-frequency numbers by Thursday" wins arguments that arguing loses.

caption.en: Fifteen minutes on the payments monolith, spent two ways.
caption.es: Quince minutos sobre el monolito de pagos, gastados de dos formas.

note.en: The predictable outcome of bringing options. You're paid to have a pick.
note.es: El resultado predecible de traer opciones. Te pagan por tener una postura.

note.en: Bottom line first. State purpose and recommendation before any supporting detail.
note.es: La conclusión primero. Di el propósito y la recomendación antes de cualquier detalle.

note.en: Rejected options belong AFTER the recommendation — they make it credible, they don't build up to it.
note.es: Las opciones rechazadas van DESPUÉS de la recomendación: la hacen creíble, no construyen hacia ella.

note.en: Adapt to how each leader preprocesses. Ignoring that reads as not knowing your audience.
note.es: Adáptate a cómo procesa cada líder. Ignorarlo se lee como no conocer a tu audiencia.

note.en: In-room debate spends credibility. A dated follow-up with data spends nothing.
note.es: Debatir en la sala gasta credibilidad. Un seguimiento con fecha y datos no gasta nada.

# Shared service template — dissent & stall log

Marcus (platform lead) is territorial about how his team builds services and sits
on the review board. Bringing this to the board cold makes him defend his
position publicly, and a public position is far harder to move than a private one.

## Pre-wire: 1:1 before the board
Goal is not to win him over. It is that he is not surprised, and that whatever
he objects to, he objects to it before an audience exists.

What came out of it, which the doc did not have:
- His actual concern isn't the template — it's that his team's services have a
  startup sequence the template's health check would fail. Concrete, fixable.
- His stated concern in past meetings ("teams should own their tooling") was the
  argument he reaches for when the specific thing has no room to be said.

→ Template gains a health-check override. → He is credited in the doc. → He is
not deciding whether to endorse it in front of eight people.

## Two weeks later: it stalled anyway
No progress, no visible opposition. Wrong question: "how do we get people to
adopt it?" Right question: **why have we stopped?** Stalls have three causes,
and the fix is different for each:

| Cause | Signal | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Missing decision | "waiting on alignment", no meeting scheduled | Force the decision — set a date and a default |
| Unavailable person | one name in every thread, no replies | Escalate for their TIME, not for a mandate |
| Ambiguous ownership | everyone agrees, nobody has it in their plan | Name one owner, in writing |

Diagnosed here: **ambiguous ownership.** Everyone agreed at the board; it is in
nobody's quarter. Not missing code, not resistance — no owner.

→ Fix: named owner (me), 3 pilot teams, dates in the plan of record.

## What I did not do
Escalate for a mandate. The decision was already made; escalating would have
converted a scheduling problem into a political one and spent Marcus's goodwill
on a problem he wasn't causing.

caption.en: Marcus sits on the review board: the pre-wire, and the stall diagnosis for when it goes quiet anyway.
caption.es: Marcus está en el comité de revisión: la pre-alineación y el diagnóstico del estancamiento si aun así se detiene.

note.en: Public surprise creates entrenched opposition. The pre-wire buys the right to be argued with privately.
note.es: La sorpresa pública crea oposición atrincherada. La pre-alineación compra el derecho a ser rebatido en privado.

note.en: The stated objection is rarely the real one. The specific concern is usually fixable in an afternoon.
note.es: La objeción declarada rara vez es la real. La preocupación específica suele arreglarse en una tarde.

note.en: The question that reframes a stall from a motivation problem into a diagnosable one.
note.es: La pregunta que replantea un estancamiento: de problema de motivación a problema diagnosticable.

note.en: Escalate for time, not for authority. Asking for a mandate when you need an hour poisons the well.
note.es: Escala por tiempo, no por autoridad. Pedir un mandato cuando necesitas una hora envenena el pozo.

note.en: The most common cause and the least dramatic. Unanimous agreement with no owner produces nothing.
note.es: La causa más común y la menos dramática. Acuerdo unánime sin dueño no produce nada.

# Two-year technical vision — 40 services, 6 teams
# Each team has its own pipeline, base image, and on-call runbook.

## Method: write five plausible strategies, forecast each 24 months out
Not to pick a winner from a list — to find where they converge. The convergence
is the vision; the divergence is what you're actually choosing between.

| # | Strategy | Where it is in 24 months |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Kubernetes everywhere** (the loud one) | Migrated. A platform team of 4 now runs the cluster; each team still has its own pipeline and base image ON k8s. The pain we started with, relocated. |
| 2 | **Serverless-first** | ~12 services fit well, 28 don't. Two operating models instead of one. Strictly worse. |
| 3 | **Standardize the pipeline + base image, leave runtimes alone** | One deploy path, one image lineage, one on-call runbook shape. 40 services, unchanged runtimes. Anyone can take any page. |
| 4 | **Full platform team owning everything** | Requires 6 engineers we don't have; becomes a ticket queue at this size. |
| 5 | **Do nothing deliberate** | 8 pipelines instead of 6. Onboarding still 3 weeks. |

## Where they converge
1, 3 and 4 all end up needing **one pipeline, one image lineage, one runbook
shape.** That convergence is the vision. Kubernetes is one possible *implementation
detail* of it — and strategy 1 shows that adopting it does not deliver the
convergence by itself. That is the argument against the loud proposal, and it
isn't "k8s is bad".

## The vision (2 years)
**Any engineer can deploy, debug and take on-call for any service, without that
team's tribal knowledge.** One pipeline. One base-image lineage. One runbook
shape. Runtime choice stays with teams.

## What we stop doing
- Stop building per-team pipelines. Immediately.
- Stop the two in-flight k8s migrations until the pipeline work lands.
- Stop treating base images as a team preference.

## The test this has to pass
Someone two orgs away, without me in the room, can read this and reject a
proposal for a seventh bespoke pipeline. If they can't, it's too vague to be a
direction — it's a wish list.

caption.en: Five strategies forecast to 2028 — and why the answer isn't the loud one ("Kubernetes everywhere").
caption.es: Cinco estrategias proyectadas a 2028, y por qué la respuesta no es la más ruidosa ("Kubernetes en todo").

note.en: Forecasting several strategies is what surfaces the invariant. Picking one first just defends the first idea.
note.es: Proyectar varias estrategias es lo que revela el invariante. Elegir una primero solo defiende la primera idea.

note.en: Forecast to the 24-month implication, not the adoption date. Most tech proposals fail at exactly this line.
note.es: Proyecta a la implicación de 24 meses, no a la fecha de adopción. La mayoría de propuestas falla justo en esta línea.

note.en: You're pricing options against their implications, not chasing or rejecting technologies.
note.es: Estás valuando opciones contra sus implicaciones, no persiguiendo ni rechazando tecnologías.

note.en: A vision that doesn't say what to stop is a wish list. This section is where it becomes a direction.
note.es: Una visión que no dice qué dejar de hacer es una lista de deseos. Esta sección la vuelve dirección.

note.en: The real test of a vision: it can reject a proposal in your absence.
note.es: La prueba real de una visión: puede rechazar una propuesta en tu ausencia.

# rollout: "event-driven by default; synchronous calls require written justification"
# The doc is polished. Posting it in #engineering is not a launch — it is an
# announcement, and it hands the loud minority an open-ended veto.

phase_1_working_group:
  who: the 4 most-AFFECTED teams, not the 4 most-supportive
  size: 6 people          # small enough to change the doc in a day
  duration: 5 days        # fast, on purpose: find what's broken before my name is on it
  mandate: "break this"
  found:
    - the payments team has 3 synchronous calls that are legally required to be
      synchronous. Policy gains an explicit exemption class, not a case-by-case plea.
    - "written justification" had no reviewer named -> would have become a queue
      pointed at me. Now: the owning team's tech lead approves, logged in the ADR.
    - no guidance on request/reply over a broker, which is what half of them need.
  # Changing the doc now is cheap. Changing it after an org-wide announcement
  # costs credibility, because it looks like retreat rather than iteration.

phase_2_org_wide_qa:
  format: doc + one 45-minute session + a comment window
  window: 10 working days   # EXPLICIT and short
  why_bounded: >
    Open-ended feedback does not converge. It lets a small number of loud
    objectors keep the decision permanently open, which is indistinguishable
    from a reversal but with none of the honesty.
  what_changes: real gaps and unworkable mechanics
  what_does_not: the decision itself — that was made, and the doc says so

phase_3_default_flips:
  date: start of next quarter
  applies_to: new services and new integrations only  # nothing retroactive
  escape_hatch: the exemption class from phase 1, self-serve, logged

phase_4_impact_review:
  when: 2 months after the flip     # scheduled NOW, in the calendar, with the doc
  measures:
    - exemptions filed, and how many were legitimate (high = policy is wrong)
    - median integration lead time, before vs after
    - incidents traced to eventual-consistency surprises
  commitment: >
    We publish this even if it says the policy was a mistake. An unmeasured
    strategy is indistinguishable from one nobody meant.

caption.en: "Event-driven by default" across 80 engineers: the rollout plan instead of posting the doc in #engineering.
caption.es: "Event-driven por defecto" en 80 ingenieros: el plan de despliegue en vez de publicar el doc en #engineering.

note.en: Supportive teams validate your doc. Affected teams break it, which is the point.
note.es: Los equipos que apoyan validan tu doc. Los afectados lo rompen, que es el objetivo.

note.en: Iterating in days with 6 people is free. Iterating after an 80-person announcement is not.
note.es: Iterar en días con 6 personas es gratis. Iterar tras anunciarlo a 80 personas no.

note.en: Any policy requiring approval needs a named approver who isn't you, or it becomes your inbox.
note.es: Toda política que requiere aprobación necesita un aprobador con nombre que no seas tú, o se vuelve tu bandeja.

note.en: A short explicit window converges. Open-ended feedback lets a loud minority stall it forever.
note.es: Una ventana corta y explícita converge. La retroalimentación abierta deja que una minoría ruidosa lo frene para siempre.

note.en: Scheduled at launch, not promised vaguely. This is what makes the strategy falsifiable.
note.es: Agendada al lanzar, no prometida vagamente. Esto es lo que hace la estrategia falsable.

# Escalation while the VP is out (2 weeks)

Partner team wants my org to freeze a migration so their launch isn't
destabilized. They need an answer today, and everyone assumes I can give one.

## The test, before answering
Borrowed authority is a loan against someone else's credibility. Spend it once in
a direction they'd have rejected and it is recalled — permanently, and reasonably.

| Bucket | Test | This case |
|---|---|---|
| **Decide** | I know their answer from precedent | — |
| **Decide + tell** | Reversible, and consistent with a stated priority | ✅ partly |
| **Do not decide alone** | Changes a commitment they made to a peer | ✅ partly |

## What I actually said today
Split it, because the "single answer" they asked for was two questions:

**Decided (the reversible part).** We pause the two riskiest migration steps for
72 hours around their launch window. This is reversible, costs us three days,
and matches a priority the VP has stated in writing twice: no launch destabilized
by platform work. I don't need her for this and I'm not pretending I asked.

**Not mine (the part that isn't).** A full freeze through their launch is 3 weeks,
which breaks the migration date the VP committed to the CTO. That commitment was
hers to make and it is hers to change. Named the boundary out loud rather than
splitting the difference: *"I can give you 72 hours today. Three weeks needs her,
and she's back Monday — I've put it on her first agenda with your context."*

Saying "I can't decide that" is not weakness; guessing on a peer commitment is
how the loan gets recalled.

## Same day, not Monday
Written summary to the VP: the decision I made, the reasoning, the priority I
leaned on, and the escalation waiting for her. Over-communicate the edge calls —
the failure mode is her hearing about my decision from the partner team's VP
first, at which point it doesn't matter whether the call was right.

caption.en: "They need an answer today": the three-bucket test for what you can decide with a VP's authority.
caption.es: "Necesitan una respuesta hoy": la prueba de tres cubos sobre qué puedes decidir con la autoridad de un VP.

note.en: The asymmetry: correct calls earn a little trust, one wrong-direction call ends the arrangement.
note.es: La asimetría: las decisiones correctas ganan algo de confianza, una en dirección equivocada termina el arreglo.

note.en: Most "I need a decision today" escalations decompose. Splitting them is the actual skill.
note.es: La mayoría de escalaciones de "necesito una decisión hoy" se descomponen. Separarlas es la habilidad real.

note.en: Alignment is internalizing their priorities well enough to make their call, citing the basis.
note.es: Alineación es internalizar sus prioridades lo suficiente para tomar su decisión, citando la base.

note.en: Splitting the difference on a peer commitment spends authority you weren't lent.
note.es: Partir la diferencia en un compromiso entre pares gasta autoridad que no te prestaron.

note.en: The one unrecoverable failure. Over-communicate edge calls the same day, not at the next 1:1.
note.es: La única falla irrecuperable. Sobrecomunica las decisiones límite el mismo día, no en el próximo 1:1.

code.snippet:
# Bet: checkout latency

Everyone agrees "performance matters," so nothing moves: it is no one's job and
it loses to the feature roadmap every planning cycle. Agreement is the problem —
it costs nothing and commits nobody.

## 1. Shape — name the bet and what winning means
**Bet:** checkout p99 from 2.1s to under 600ms by end of Q3.
**Not:** "improve checkout performance."

Public and numeric on purpose. A named target with a date forces real resourcing,
because it can be visibly missed. "Performance matters" cannot be missed, which
is exactly why it never gets staffed.

**What winning is worth,** so the number isn't arbitrary: our own funnel data puts
conversion loss at ~0.4% per 100ms above 800ms → ~$2.1M/yr at 2.1s.
**What losing looks like:** we get to ~900ms, the remaining cost is in the payment
provider's API, and we stop. Written down now, so a partial result is scored as a
partial result instead of relabelled a success.

## 2. Sponsor — before committing anyone
An empowered sponsor: **VP Product** (owns the conversion metric, has budget, sits
in the planning meeting where this would otherwise be cut).

Asked for three things explicitly, and got them in writing:
- 3 engineers for 2 quarters, named, not "as available"
- the bet appears in HER plan of record, not only in engineering's
- **she has agreed to defend it in mid-quarter replanning** — the specific moment
  bets die

Without that third one I do not start. An unsponsored bet is the first thing cut
in a reorg, and it burns the engineers who staffed it — they lose two quarters of
visible work and learn not to volunteer next time.

## 3. Commit — only now
Team named, kickoff scheduled, scoreboard published where anyone can read it:
p99 weekly, conversion weekly, remaining hypotheses ranked.

## Sequence
shape → sponsor → commit. Reversing the last two is the common failure: staff it
first, hunt for air cover later, and discover in week nine there wasn't any.

caption.en: 2.1s checkout p99 that everyone agrees matters and nobody owns: shape → sponsor → commit.
caption.es: Un p99 de 2.1s en checkout que todos dicen que importa y nadie posee: dar forma → patrocinio → comprometer.

note.en: Universal agreement with no owner is the stable state. It feels like progress and produces nothing.
note.es: El acuerdo universal sin dueño es el estado estable. Se siente como progreso y no produce nada.

note.en: Public stakes are the mechanism. A target that can't be missed can't be resourced.
note.es: Las apuestas públicas son el mecanismo. Un objetivo que no se puede fallar no se puede financiar.

note.en: Define the loss condition up front, or a partial result gets relabelled a win and you learn nothing.
note.es: Define la condición de pérdida desde el inicio, o un resultado parcial se reetiqueta como éxito y no aprendes nada.

note.en: The precise moment bets die. A sponsor who hasn't agreed to this hasn't sponsored anything.
note.es: El momento exacto en que mueren las apuestas. Un patrocinador que no aceptó esto no ha patrocinado nada.

note.en: Sequence isn't bureaucracy. Sponsorship secured after staffing is sponsorship you don't have.
note.es: La secuencia no es burocracia. Patrocinio conseguido después de asignar gente es patrocinio que no tienes.
